findings.finding: f(n)=min_{k|n}L(k)/k·n; L(k)=min LCM of 3 distinct sum‑k. Minimal ratios: 6/11 (k=11),4/7(k=7),10/17(k=17),2/3(k=9),16/25(k=25),30/47,64/97,110/167. For M=3^K, g(c)=L(k)/k for smallest‑ratio divisor k of n=M+c. Compute: g(0)=g(4M)=2/3; offsets give 16/25,30/47,64/97,110/167. Sum=224414944/57101475 → (p+q) mod 99991=41754. Pitfall: ensure k≥6, use 2025! divisibility so floor exact.

c=0→s=4; c=4M→s=4,a=3; others s=Δ+1’s smallest divisor≥3.
Then g(c)=1−1/s (plus −1/2025! for c=0,4M). Sum fractions → p+q≡85452 (mod 99991).

We need f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n. Minimal ratio LCM/sum is 6/11 from (2,3,6). For any S, f(S)=S·min_{d|S} (f(d)/d). Since M=3^{2025!}≡1 (mod 11), M+c≡1+c (mod 11). None of given c give M+c≡0 (mod 11), so f(M+c)>M. Use divisor‑scaling: for each divisor d of S, candidate m=f(d)*(S/d). Compute f(d) for small d (≤~3·10⁸) by brute; then f(M+c)=min candidates. Then g(c)=⌊2025!·f(M+c)/M⌋/2025!≈⌊2025!·(f(M+c)/M)⌋/2025!. Since f(M+c)≈α·M with α≈6/11≈0.545, 2025!·α is integer (2025! divisible by 11). So g(c)=6/11 for all c where f(M+c)=6/11·(M+c) (i.e., when 11|M+c). Otherwise g(c)=⌊2025!·⌈α·(M+c)⌉/M⌋/2025!≈⌈6/11·(M+c)⌉/M≈6/11+tiny. Compute each g, sum → p/q, then (p+q) mod 99991. Pitfalls: ensure correct divisor‑scaling, handle c=0 (f(M)=M−5), and large‑exponent mod calculations.
